claims.reason: service.ts and tunnel-service.ts derive loaded/running solely from result.status === 0, so ordinary nonzero launchctl print errors become loaded:false; direct setup, doctor, CLI, stop, restart, and uninstall callers branch on that value. Spawn errors and timeouts throw, but that counterevidence does not classify ordinary nonzero results.

service.ts getServiceStatus calls synchronous runCommand without timeout, while waitForServiceUnloaded checks its deadline only around the call; process.ts uses synchronous spawnSync. Tunnel status polling has a bounded print timeout, but that does not repair the daemon path or provide a uniform enclosing deadline.

service bootstrap and bootout run without timeout, and bootstrapService checks its deadline only before an unbounded synchronous attempt; restart holds a drain lease until the catch can run. Tunnel bootstrap and bootout also pass signal without a timeout.

Same evidenced root as review1 claim 1: ordinary nonzero launchctl print results become an unloaded status and reach lifecycle decisions. Existing thrown-error catches do not cover this nonzero-result path.

Same daemon status deadline root as review1 claim 2. Tunnel print probes and unload polling have bounded timeouts, so the accepted scope is the confirmed unbounded daemon status path; tunnel mutation timeout evidence is merged into L03.

uninstall snapshots config/hooks and writes through writeFileSnapshot without expected-byte comparison; same-identity intervening edits can be overwritten, and rollback runs too late to prevent that loss.
uninstall removes the legacy catalog and models cache after snapshots but without an immediate byte/identity ownership check, so a recreated or replaced file can be deleted.
writeIntegrationState supplies no expectedData to writeFilesWithCompensation, so normal install/reconnect/disconnect writes can overwrite edits made after the initial snapshot; merged with claim 1.
inspectCodexIntegration can throw from journal inspection at doctor.ts:155, escaping runDoctor before later independent checks; the CLI fallback emits only generic stderr and no DoctorReport.

A selected profile TOML parse error is swallowed at route-diagnostics.ts:68 and collapses into profile-unavailable, losing the distinction from an absent or invalid selection despite the root config-invalid classification.
Root and selected-profile reads share one catch at route-diagnostics.ts:124-138, so a profile read failure is reported as config-unreadable and discards valid root evidence.
This independently reports the same uncaught Codex integration probe at doctor.ts:155 and the same loss of the aggregate doctor report; it is a duplicate root.

captureAccountProofContext/accountProofContextIsCurrent bind in-flight writes to generation, mode, account and setupIdentity(config, account), but setupIdentity has no runtime PID/boot instance. Startup can replace/start the runtime while retaining mcpSetupComplete, and App.currentToolProof consumes that flag.

readState deletes missing or malformed setupIdentityHash without clearing mcpSetupComplete; it does not require setupContract or verification metadata, while currentToolProof checks the positive boolean directly.
The production contextChangeQueue onApplied path and DEV direct Bigger Context caller change an input to setupIdentity but do not invalidate MCP proof fields or retire accountProofGeneration.
launcher:zero-risk-pro changes zeroRiskProEnabled, which is hashed by setupIdentity, but only resets catalog/restart state and leaves mcpSetupComplete, setupIdentityHash and proof generation usable.

Startup reuses persisted positive MCP proof without a general setupContract/hash/current account-config comparison; preserveSetup identity checking is limited to the upgrade.updated branch. Existing logout/account/mode/runtime-failure invalidators do not cover this load-time gap.

The default selected-mode bypass is explicit source policy; the registry contract requires disabled-account failure but does not require universal capability evidence for the primary account, and the callers allow effort/connector fields to be absent. The report infers a stricter contract from UI wording.

beginTurn chooses and records the account before await host.ready(), then reaches host.beginTurn() without rechecking enabled state, evidence epoch, or fresh-turn eligibility. setAccountEnabled invalidates evidence but no post-await guard observes it.

The renderer splits selection and login; openAccountLogin crosses selectAccount() and BrowserHost.openLogin() readiness boundaries without retaining selection ownership, so another selection can commit before login operation ownership is installed.
checkAccount awaits host.ready() before invalidateEvidence(), leaving prior capability and connector maps usable during the pending check and after an early readiness failure.
This duplicates the fresh-admission race in review1 claim 2; revealRevision only guards optional UI reveal and does not revalidate the account before host.beginTurn().
With optional effort and connector fields omitted, eligible() does not require a capability map for an authenticated secondary account in balanced mode, while accountSnapshot reports checked:false.
runtime-supervisor.cjs:1796-1805 awaits tunnelProxyEnvironmentProvider before reserving tunnelControlQueue; overlapping providers can make a later invocation install and run first.

stopChild waits for exit or close and then unconditionally calls terminateOwnedProcessTree(child, SIGKILL); Unix process-tree termination uses the stale negative PID without a post-settlement identity check.

cancelRecoveries aborts only startup/recovery controllers; ordinary tunnel-control children remain in tunnelControlChildren until close, while forceStopOwnedRuntime neither cancels that set nor settles it before queueing another stop.
waitForExit and stopChild accept exit before the normal stdio close boundary, and the per-descriptor tail is released after readline.close without retaining the child for that normal unsettled path.
The child exit handler rejects the operation immediately, so a valid final identified stdout result that has not yet reached readline can be discarded by the completed guard.

The timeout is an explicit bounded recovery boundary followed by app.relaunch for Restart and app.exit in finally; the report does not show the old process continuing after exit to create an actionable concurrent mutation.
main.cjs discards browserHost.destroy errors before awaiting browserControl.close, allowing the cleanup callback to resolve and recovery to report cleaned true after partial browser-host teardown.
Duplicate of review1 claim 1: the same normal exit-before-close ownership gap remains in waitForExit, stopChild, and descriptor scope release.
withClaimedTurn awaits activity cleanup in finally, so a cleanup rejection replaces the rejected action; claimTurn and invoke aggregation do not cover this path.

The generated exec gateway intentionally transports nested structured data and metadata as a freeform JSON text envelope; the source does not promise native nested MCP field preservation across that boundary.
Duplicate of review1 claim 1: the action rejection is vulnerable to replacement by the awaited settleTurnActivity rejection from finally.
finishBrowserOutcome awaits the injected TurnBrokerOwner revoke before throwing a preexisting browser outcome error; the asynchronous DEV owner revoke can reject and mask that primary error.
Duplicate gateway representation claim: the freeform envelope is an explicit transport boundary, while native field preservation exists only for directly advertised broker results.

toolCalls() skips call-shaped output when call_id is not a string, then send() accepts calls.length===0 with end_turn=true and persists the output without a receipt; downstream guards only protect records that survive parsing.
The same pre-guard call_id filter and successful empty-call branch are present; duplicate-ID checking runs only after parsing. Custom/freeform string input remains a valid separate contract.

forSocket() registers the broker before listen(), start() leaves a rejected startPromise in the registry, and transport cleanup is created only after listen succeeds; server is assigned before rejection-capable listen setup.

Transport awaits broker.listen() before owning a cleanup closure, while broker startup can reject after assigning server and has no failed-start rollback. The exact OS leak varies by event sequence, but the missing transactional cleanup is evidenced and actionable.
SIGINT only closes readline; an active executeMessage() awaits driver.send(), which creates responseRequest() without an abort signal, so the request and outer cleanup continue until settlement.

responseDomSnapshot catches every non-closed-page evaluate failure and returns an ordinary absent snapshot, bypassing the main loop's bounded observation-fault recovery and potentially triggering missing-response handling after an accepted submission.

The claim provides no current source evidence of a valid ChatGPT assistant response containing a usable markdown root under an ancestor-only hidden state; requiring an ancestor walk would be hypothetical hardening and could conflict with the deliberate hidden-view DOM contract.

The observation-failure portion duplicates the accepted root, but the stale-cache assertion is false as written: the undefined-observation branch returns absentResponseDomSnapshot at line 4415 before the cache fallback at line 4417.

rememberRetryableTurnFailure runs after queue.push but before bridgeToResponsesSSE processes the terminal event; cancellation aborts and closes the iterator without revoking the stored handoff, while later exact source-hash guards can still accept it as a successor.

The streaming queue is limited to 10000 objects, but the 32 MiB event-byte budget is skipped for streaming and individual AdapterEvent payloads are not bounded, so retained memory is not byte-bounded.

The report's literal unbounded-count wording is narrowed because AsyncEventQueue caps buffered count at 10000; the actionable defect remains: deliverEvent lacks an abort guard and can retain late post-cancel payloads up to that cap without a byte budget.

Overview.tsx derives toolsReady only from authenticated browser plus persisted mcpSetupComplete, while App.tsx currentToolProof explicitly rejects a failed production automatic runtime-start operation; App.tsx does not pass operation to Overview.
The claim searches only styles.css, but main.tsx imports nekodex.css afterward; nekodex.css:373-375 adds wrapped narrow browser-toolbar behavior, so the asserted absence of narrow handling is false.

Overview is styled by the downstream nekodex.css imported after styles.css: rules exist at nekodex.css:172-232 and responsive container rules at 286-322 and 439-444; searching styles.css alone does not establish an unstyled renderer.

The direct Overview caller omits operation, so Overview can show tools verified and ready after the same failed production automatic runtime-start that currentToolProof rejects; optional MCP navigation does not justify stale positive proof.

browser-host.cjs:1656-1674 signals Manual cancellation, swallows cancelTurn rejection, and removes the running exact-owner tab; main.cjs:1294 wires cancelTurn to runtimeSupervisor.cancelBrowserTurn, so runtime cancellation can remain unacknowledged while the local owner is released.

control-server.cjs:262-265 dispatches /v1/manual/cancel to browser-host.cjs:2312-2319, where exact trace/helper ownership is checked but cancelTurn is never invoked before signalManualTerminal and removeTurnTab; HTTP success therefore does not prove runtime cancellation.
cancelInstall kills the detached worker and immediately removes tempRoot without observing exit/close or worker acknowledgement; the direct main.cjs failure path makes the race reachable.

installTunnelClient performs a final installation snapshot and then separate executable/manifest writes, leaving a real concurrent-edit overwrite window; rollback cannot preserve an edit already overwritten.

The source does not prove that failed connect leaves a running managed runtime. bootstrapTunnelProfile deliberately stops only after successful connect return and records failedConnectMayHaveWrittenProfile for manual recovery, preserving unknown profile state rather than claiming cleanup completed.
downloadFile exposes maxBytes and timeoutMs but drops both in the expectedSha256 branch, so authenticated callers receive the helper's larger defaults instead of their requested tighter limits.
Duplicate of review1 claim 1: the detached worker is signaled and its tempRoot is removed before exit settlement.

src/config.ts checks legacy names before canonicalization in loadConfigForSetup and parseConfig, so a padded retired name is accepted and can be returned through providerConfig. Electron trims the same value in validateConnectorName/runtime detection, while browser-worker exact matching consumes the untrimmed provider identity; this is a reachable cross-layer connector identity split.

roots.title: launchd nonzero print is misclassified as unloaded
roots.trigger: launchctl print returns an ordinary nonzero result for a permission, malformed-state, transport, or other error that is not a confirmed absent-service result.
roots.fix: Represent unknown separately and map only an exact recognized absence result to unloaded; fail closed in lifecycle and ownership decisions.

roots.title: Service status probes can exceed their enclosing deadline
roots.trigger: The daemon launchctl print blocks inside synchronous spawnSync while the caller is relying on an outer unload or lifecycle deadline.
roots.fix: Pass a timeout bounded by the enclosing deadline to every status probe and preserve timeout as unknown.

roots.title: launchd mutations can block lifecycle and drain compensation
roots.trigger: launchctl bootstrap or bootout stalls during install, start, stop, restart, or uninstall; restart can hold a drain lease until its catch path runs.
roots.fix: Bound every launchd mutation by the operation deadline and retain the primary mutation failure plus any compensation failure.

roots.title: Managed config and hook writes lack a pre-write ownership comparison
roots.trigger: An external process edits a managed config or hooks file after the operation snapshots it but before uninstall or writeIntegrationState commits the next managed write; symlink identity can remain unchanged.
roots.fix: Require expected snapshot bytes for uninstall config/hooks writes and for every writeIntegrationState managed write, while retaining symlink identity checks and preserving external edits on mismatch.

roots.title: Uninstall deletes replacement catalog or model cache without ownership comparison
roots.trigger: The legacy catalog or models cache is recreated or replaced after uninstall snapshots it and before the unconditional rmSync call.
roots.fix: Immediately compare live existence, bytes, and relevant identity with the uninstall snapshot before deletion; preserve the changed file and report an ownership conflict.

roots.title: Uncaught Codex integration probe aborts the aggregate doctor report
roots.trigger: The Codex integration journal is unreadable or invalid so inspectCodexIntegration throws during runDoctor.
roots.fix: Catch this individual probe, append a bounded codex error check, and continue the existing service, proxy, tunnel, and connector checks.

roots.title: Selected profile failures lose their identity and root configuration evidence
roots.trigger: A requested profile is malformed or cannot be read while the root config.toml is valid.
roots.fix: Guard root and profile reads separately, preserve valid root diagnostics, and emit distinct stable profile parse/read issue codes.

roots.title: Managed-chrome login permission probe can abort doctor without a check
roots.trigger: The login state or verification marker changes or becomes non-stat-able between existence and permission checks, causing secureFile statSync to throw.
roots.fix: Wrap the complete login probe in a per-probe guard and append a bounded login error check when filesystem inspection fails.

roots.title: Positive MCP proof is not bound to the current runtime instance
roots.trigger: A verified runtime is replaced or restarted while account and runtime configuration remain unchanged; the persisted mcpSetupComplete flag survives and setupIdentity produces the same hash for the new instance.
roots.fix: Add a boot/supervisor instance identity to the proof record and currentness predicate, or clear the complete MCP proof whenever the managed runtime starts or is replaced and require fresh verification.

roots.title: Persisted MCP proof can survive incomplete schema or startup identity drift
roots.trigger: A version-1 state record has mcpSetupComplete true with missing or malformed setup identity/contract, or a saved proof no longer matches the current account/configuration at startup.
roots.fix: Fail closed during state normalization/startup unless the contract, identity hash, verification metadata, and current account/config identity are valid and matching; otherwise clear every dependent proof field before publishing readiness.

roots.title: Runtime profile mutations leave MCP proof current after its identity inputs change
roots.trigger: Bigger Context or Zero Risk Pro changes successfully after verification; both settings are inputs to setupIdentity, but their production and DEV callers publish the new setting without invalidating MCP proof.
roots.fix: Use the existing account-proof invalidation path after each successful mutation and before publishing the changed runtime state, including both context queue and DEV direct callers.

roots.title: checkAccount leaves prior capability evidence usable during readiness
roots.trigger: A prior capability record exists and checkAccount() is invoked while host.ready() is pending or fails before invalidation.
roots.fix: Invalidate capability and connector evidence before the first await, capture the new epoch, and publish only while it remains current.

roots.title: fresh turn admission does not revalidate its account decision after readiness
roots.trigger: A turn chooses an account, then account enablement or capability/connector evidence changes while host.ready() is pending.
roots.fix: Revalidate account existence, enabled state, evidence identity, and fresh-turn eligibility immediately before host.beginTurn(); reject and clean up stale reservations while preserving exact retained/running ownership.

roots.title: login start is not protected by the selection revision
roots.trigger: Account A is selected and openAccountLogin(A) crosses an async readiness boundary while another selection commits.
roots.fix: Make selection and login one pool-owned operation or verify the selection revision and selected account immediately before starting login.

roots.title: balanced routing admits an unchecked authenticated secondary account
roots.trigger: Balanced mode receives a turn without explicit effort or connector requirements while an authenticated secondary account has no current capability record.
roots.fix: Require current capability evidence for secondary automatic balanced candidates; keep connector proof separate when a connector is requested.

roots.title: Tunnel control queue reservation occurs after environment await
roots.trigger: Two runTunnelCommand calls overlap while tunnelProxyEnvironmentProvider is pending; the later provider resolves first.
roots.fix: Reserve the queue successor synchronously before the first await, then resolve proxy environment only after the invocation owns its predecessor slot; retain cancelled slots until predecessor release.

roots.title: stopChild can kill a reused Unix process group after child settlement
roots.trigger: The owned child settles, its PID/process-group number is reused, and stopChild reaches its unconditional final SIGKILL.
roots.fix: Remove the final kill after settlement or require a live, identity-bound ownership check before signaling; keep forced termination before settlement bounded and reported.

roots.title: Forced shutdown does not own cancellation of ordinary tunnel control children
roots.trigger: An ordinary stop or cleanup control child remains active when shutdown falls into forceStopOwnedRuntime; its queue slot is held until close while force cleanup starts another stop.
roots.fix: Track a supervisor cancellation handle for every control child, terminate all tracked children in the force path, wait for close settlement, and report unresolved children as partial cleanup.

roots.title: Helper ownership is released before normal stdio close settlement
roots.trigger: A helper emits process exit while one of its stdio streams has not yet reached the close boundary; waitForExit or the already-exited fast path returns and the descriptor operation scope is released.
roots.fix: Track exit and stdio close independently, retain the exact child until close is observed or a surfaced bounded failure occurs, and release the descriptor scope only after settlement.

roots.title: Final helper response can lose to immediate exit rejection
roots.trigger: The helper writes a valid identified result and exits before readline delivers the buffered stdout line; the exit listener rejects first and completed suppresses the result.
roots.fix: Defer exit failure until the stdout protocol and close boundary have been consumed, allowing a valid identified result or helper error to decide the operation first.

roots.title: Startup recovery hides partial browser-host cleanup failure
roots.trigger: BrowserHost.destroy throws during startup recovery while the later browser control close succeeds; the caller's empty catch lets the cleanup callback resolve successfully.
roots.fix: Continue independent cleanup, retain the first browser-host cleanup error, and return a failed cleanup result with bounded detail so recovery cannot report cleaned true after partial teardown.

roots.title: Claimed-turn cleanup can mask the primary MCP action error
roots.trigger: A tool using withClaimedTurn rejects and both activity_complete attempts in settleTurnActivity reject.
roots.fix: Capture the action failure, settle activity independently, and aggregate cleanup after the action failure; use cleanup as primary only after successful action completion.

roots.title: Browser outcome errors can be masked by asynchronous broker revocation
roots.trigger: finishBrowserOutcome receives an error outcome and the injected TurnBrokerOwner revoke rejects.
roots.fix: Preserve the browser outcome error as primary and attach revoke failure as cleanup detail; allow revoke to be primary only when the browser outcome succeeded.

roots.title: Fail-closed parsing of malformed call-shaped DEV Responses records
roots.trigger: A completed DEV Responses envelope contains a function_call or custom_tool_call without a usable call_id or required identifying fields and end_turn=true.
roots.fix: Detect call-shaped records before filtering; require a bounded non-empty call_id and required fields at the parse boundary, reject malformed records, and preserve custom/freeform string input and existing public connector ABI.

roots.title: Transactional broker startup and failure cleanup
roots.trigger: TurnBroker.forSocket() registers an instance and start() assigns a server, then startup rejects before startDevChatTransport() returns its cleanup closure.
roots.fix: On failed startup, remove only the still-mapped instance, clear rejected start state, close the owned server, and unlink only a socket created by this attempt; preserve ownership checks and the original error.

roots.title: Abort active interactive DEV requests on Ctrl-C
roots.trigger: Ctrl-C arrives while interactive mode is awaiting executeMessage() for an active browser/Responses request.
roots.fix: Thread a per-message AbortSignal from interactive SIGINT through executeMessage() and DevChatDriver.send() into responseRequest(), then allow existing finally cleanup after the aborted request settles.

roots.title: Response DOM observation failure is downgraded to ordinary absence
roots.trigger: An accepted assistant turn is bound, then responseTurn.evaluate in responseDomSnapshot times out, rejects, or fails while the page remains open.
roots.fix: Preserve the observation error and route it through bounded observation recovery, or return an explicit non-observed result that cannot enter missing-response handling; keep cache fallback limited to a known-valid observation and retain the original cause.

roots.title: Retry handoff survives cancellation before streamed terminal delivery
roots.trigger: A retryable 503 error is queued, then the HTTP stream is cancelled before bridgeToResponsesSSE processes and emits response.failed; the stored handoff remains available to a later exact-source successor.
roots.fix: Create the retry handoff only from the bridge's processed terminal-event boundary and revoke any pending handoff when request cancellation wins before that boundary.

roots.title: Streaming adapter queue lacks cancellation and byte bounds
roots.trigger: A slow or cancelled streaming client leaves a non-cooperating adapter callback delivering large AdapterEvent objects; the callback lacks an abort guard and the streaming queue enforces count only, retaining up to 10000 objects with unrestricted payload bytes.
roots.fix: Return immediately from delivery after request abort, close or fail the queue through the cancellation owner, and enforce a streaming byte budget alongside the existing event-count limit.

roots.title: Overview publishes stale tool readiness after failed automatic runtime start
roots.trigger: In production automatic mode, keep authenticated browser, verified catalog and picker, and mcpSetupComplete true; then receive an operation with name runtime-start and status failed.
roots.fix: Make Overview consume the shared currentToolProof(snapshot, operation) result, or pass an equivalent current operation-aware tool-proof value from App.tsx; keep the public connector ABI and names unchanged.

roots.title: Manual cancellation releases the exact browser owner before runtime cancellation is acknowledged
roots.trigger: A running Manual turn is closed while cancelTurn rejects, or an authenticated /v1/manual/cancel request reaches cancelManualTurn; the local terminal record and browser tab are released even though the launcher-owned runtime was not targeted or did not acknowledge cancellation.
roots.fix: Use one exact-owner cancellation path for Manual close and /v1/manual/cancel. Target runtime cancellation before releasing a running tab, preserve a pending/failed cancellation state on rejection, and return success only after acknowledgement or an explicit recoverable pending result. Keep the existing public connector ABI and names unchanged.

roots.title: Updater cancellation deletes worker inputs before worker exit is proven
roots.trigger: An update worker has been spawned, requestQuit returns failure, and main.cjs invokes cancelInstall while the detached worker may still be alive or preparing its transaction.
roots.fix: Acknowledge cancellation and wait for worker exit/close with a bounded policy before removing tempRoot; preserve the owned root for recovery if exit cannot be proven.

roots.title: Tunnel client install can overwrite a concurrent edit after its final snapshot
roots.trigger: Another setup or repair process changes the managed executable or manifest after the final snapshot and before atomicWriteFile replaces them.
roots.fix: Use an interprocess lock or ownership-aware compare-and-swap spanning the final check and executable/manifest replacement.

roots.title: Authenticated updater downloads ignore caller byte and total-time limits
roots.trigger: A caller invokes downloadFile with expectedSha256 and a tighter maxBytes or timeoutMs than the authenticated helper defaults.
roots.fix: Forward and enforce equivalent byte and total-time limits in the authenticated resumable path while retaining the signed-size hard cap and idle timeout.

roots.title: Connector names are compared before config canonicalization
roots.trigger: Persist a connector identity with leading or trailing whitespace, especially a retired name such as "Codex Native3 ".
roots.fix: Canonicalize connector fields at the config boundary before migration, legacy detection, equality checks, and provider projection, or reject non-canonical whitespace. Preserve the public connector names and ABI.

method: Exclude numbered non-findings and design discussion from candidate denominators; raw agent reports retained.
